# nagios_nna_check (Resource)

Manages a Nagios Network Analyzer alert check - a warning/critical threshold evaluated against a metric on a flow source or source group. This is Network Analyzer's closest analog to a Nagios XI service check.

Network Analyzer serves four check types behind one endpoint, selected by `check_type`, each targeting a different kind of object with its own metric set:

| `check_type` | `object_type` | `metric` |
|---|---|---|
| `flow_source` (default) | `source`, `sourcegroup` | `bytes`, `flows`, `packets`, `pps`, `bps`, `bpp`, `abnormal_behavior` |
| `nmap` | `scheduled_scan` | `ports_open`, `ports_closed` |
| `suricata` | `signature_id` | `alert_count` |
| `system` | `cpu` | `cpu_usage` |
| `system` | `memory` | `used_percent`, `swap_percent` |
| `system` | `drive` | `percent`, `available` |
| `system` | `workers` | `online` |

Network Analyzer accepts any combination of these without complaint, so this resource rejects mismatched pairings at plan time. `suricata` checks additionally require `lookback_period` and `check_frequency`; `system` checks have no target object, so `object_id` must be omitted for them.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "nagios_nna_source" "core_switch" {
  name        = "core-switch-netflow"
  port        = 9995
  flowtype    = "netflow"
  lifetime    = "30"
  description = "NetFlow export from the core switch"
}

# Alert when HTTPS traffic from the core switch gets unusually heavy.
resource "nagios_nna_check" "https_volume" {
  name        = "core-switch-https-volume"
  object_type = "source"
  object_id   = nagios_nna_source.core_switch.id

  metric             = "bps"
  warning_threshold  = "100000000"
  critical_threshold = "500000000"

  queries = [{
    location       = "destination"
    location_type  = "port"
    location_bool  = "is"
    location_value = "443"
  }]
}

# Alert when a host's memory use gets high. System checks have no target
# object, so object_id is omitted.
resource "nagios_nna_check" "analyzer_swap" {
  name        = "analyzer-swap-usage"
  check_type  = "system"
  object_type = "memory"
  metric      = "swap_percent"

  warning_threshold  = "50"
  critical_threshold = "80"
}

# Alert when a Suricata signature fires too often. lookback_period and
# check_frequency are required for suricata checks.
resource "nagios_nna_check" "ssh_scan_alerts" {
  name        = "ssh-scan-alerts"
  check_type  = "suricata"
  object_type = "signature_id"
  object_id   = 2001219
  metric      = "alert_count"

  warning_threshold  = "10"
  critical_threshold = "50"
  lookback_period    = "1d"
  check_frequency    = "Hourly"
}

# Alert when an nmap scheduled scan finds too many open ports. object_id is the
# scan's ID inside Network Analyzer.
resource "nagios_nna_check" "dmz_open_ports" {
  name        = "dmz-open-ports"
  check_type  = "nmap"
  object_type = "scheduled_scan"
  object_id   = 3
  metric      = "ports_open"

  warning_threshold  = "20"
  critical_threshold = "40"
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `metric` (String) The metric to evaluate the thresholds against; the valid values depend on `check_type` (and, for `system`, `object_type`) - see the resource description. Thresholds are ignored for the `abnormal_behavior` metric.
- `name` (String) The name of this check.
- `object_type` (String) What the check targets. For `flow_source`: `source` for a single flow source or `sourcegroup` for a source group. For `nmap`: `scheduled_scan`. For `suricata`: `signature_id`. For `system`: `cpu`, `memory`, `drive` or `workers`.

### Optional

- `alert_commands` (Set of Number) IDs of Network Analyzer commands to run when this check changes state.
- `alert_nagios_servers` (Set of Number) IDs of Network Analyzer Nagios server definitions to send passive check results to.
- `alert_snmp_receivers` (Set of Number) IDs of Network Analyzer SNMP trap receivers to notify.
- `alert_users` (Set of Number) IDs of `nagios_nna_user` accounts to notify when this check changes state.
- `check_frequency` (String) How often a `suricata` check runs: `5min`, `Hourly`, `Daily`, `Weekly`, `Monthly` or `Yearly`. Required for `suricata` checks and invalid for every other type.
- `check_type` (String) The kind of check, fixed for the life of the check (changing it replaces the check): `flow_source` (the default), `nmap`, `suricata` or `system`. Determines which `object_type` and `metric` values are valid - see the resource description.
- `critical_threshold` (String) The critical threshold, in Nagios range syntax. Same conventions as `warning_threshold`.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether this check is actively evaluated. A newly created check always starts enabled, since Network Analyzer ignores this on create; set to false to have Terraform disable it immediately afterwards.
- `lookback_period` (String) How far back a `suricata` check counts alerts: `1d`, `7d`, `30d`, `90d`, `180d` or `365d`. Required for `suricata` checks and invalid for every other type.
- `object_id` (Number) The ID of the object this check evaluates: a `nagios_nna_source` or `nagios_nna_source_group` for `flow_source`, an nmap scheduled scan for `nmap`, a Suricata signature ID for `suricata`. Required for those types and must be omitted for `system` checks, which have no target object (Network Analyzer reports `-1`). Network Analyzer does not validate this reference, so an ID that doesn't exist is accepted on write and simply yields a check that never produces a result - prefer interpolating another resource's `id` over hardcoding a number where one exists.
- `queries` (Attributes List) Traffic filter clauses narrowing what this check measures. Network Analyzer compiles these server-side into the `raw_query` filter expression below and never returns them, so - unlike every other attribute here - changes made outside Terraform to the underlying filter cannot be detected; `raw_query` is the observable result of what was last applied. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--queries))
- `warning_threshold` (String) The warning threshold, in Nagios range syntax (e.g. `1000`, `10:20`, `~:500`, `@10:20`). Omit the attribute entirely for no warning threshold - Network Analyzer stores an empty threshold as null and would report it back as unset, so an explicitly empty string is rejected here rather than causing a permanent diff.

### Read-Only

- `id` (Number) The numeric ID Network Analyzer assigns this check. Unlike this provider's XI resources, Network Analyzer addresses objects by ID rather than name.
- `last_code` (Number) The Nagios return code from the last run (0 OK, 1 warning, 2 critical, 3 unknown). Null until it first runs.
- `last_output` (String) The status text from the last run. Empty until it first runs.
- `last_run` (String) When this check last ran. Empty until it first runs.
- `last_value` (String) The metric value recorded the last time this check ran. Empty until it first runs.
- `raw_query` (String) The filter expression Network Analyzer stored for this check: for `flow_source` checks, the traffic filter compiled from `queries` (e.g. `src port 443`); for `suricata` checks, the encoded `lookback_period`/`check_frequency` (e.g. `frequency=Hourly&lookback_period=7d`). Read-only.

<a id="nestedatt--queries"></a>
### Nested Schema for `queries`

Required:

- `location` (String) Which end of the flow to match: `source`, `destination`, or `destination_or_source`.
- `location_bool` (String) Whether the clause matches (`is`) or excludes (`is_not`).
- `location_type` (String) What kind of value to match: `port`, `ip`, or `network`.
- `location_value` (String) The value to match - a port number, an IPv4 address, or a CIDR network, according to `location_type`.
